newsitem.title: INDONESIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - Nov 29.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - Nov 29.

text.p: The following are the leading stories in the Indonesian press on November 29. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
President Suharto said the nation's teachers should be highly respected because they are important for dealing with the changing times that the nation faces.
The House of Representatives (DPR) Budgetary Commission has proposed raising the 1997/98 budget by 13 percent compared to this year's budget to 102 trillion rupiah ($43.1 billion).

An Indonesian Catholic priest Ignatius Sandyawan Sumardi, who is under investigation for harbouring activists currently facing subversion charges, has been awarded the presitigious Yap Thiam Hien human rights award.

Indonesian Foreign Minister Ali Alatas said the United Nations Security Council needed to be reformed as it was not geographically balanced and needed to be based on more objective critera. Alatas was speaking during a ceremony at which he received an honourary doctorate from Diponegoro University in Semarang, Central Java.
Government experts predict there will be 225,000 foreign workers in Indonesia earning $11.8 billion by the year 2000 compared with the current 57,000 foreign workers earning $2.4 billion.
